Create one fully composed illustrated interior, 1:2 portrait, twice as tall as wide: the Moosylvania lobby, a marketing agency inside a converted Gothic church in Maplewood, St. Louis, drawn as a LARGE explorable scene, like a game map that a visitor scrolls up and down through. Reference 2, marked COMPOSITION DRAFT, is the approved draft of this exact scene: keep its camera (a high overhead three-quarter view looking straight down the length of the nave, the long walls rising along the left and right edges), its flat illustration style and bright palette, its scale, and the design and arrangement of everything this list does not change. Use reference 1 only for flat shape language and the palette. References 3, 4 and 5 are photographs of the real lobby: 3 looks toward the entrance end (the twin curved staircases, the mezzanine loft, the glass-walled offices beneath it), 4 looks at the front desk and its frosted glass moose wall, 5 looks down from above the area behind the front desk. Redraw the draft as this TALLER picture, with these changes only: 1. THE LOFT IS MUCH BIGGER. The mezzanine loft at the top becomes a large open lounge workspace, about as deep as the round-sofa area and filling roughly the top third of the picture, reaching back to the end wall with the big pointed stained-glass window. On it stand about eight pale wood desks loosely arranged like a lounge working space, not in a row: some alone, some in pairs, some turned at an angle, each with a teal task chair, with clear floor between them to walk around; plus two soft lounge armchairs with a small side table, one low bookshelf and a few potted plants. FOUR of the desks, spread across the loft (two on the left half, two on the right half), each carry a desktop computer whose screen glows softly with plain colour; the other desks hold only a closed laptop, a lamp or books, with no screen. The loft's front edge keeps its steel railing; the two curved staircases still sweep up to it in mirror image from beside the round sofas; the two glass-walled offices and the arched double front doors between them stay beneath the loft's front edge, clearly visible. 2. THE MEETING AREA RUNS TO THE BOTTOM EDGE. The raised maple platform behind the moose glass wall spans the nave from wall to wall and simply continues to the bottom edge of the picture, where the picture ends; the chancel's end wall is behind the viewer and not shown. No steps down, no lower floor and no glass partitions at the bottom or sides of the platform; its only steps are the two short flights up from the nave, one on each side of the moose glass wall. Keep the long mustard-yellow sofa, the low charcoal table and the four dark armchairs, grouped facing the TV, with open platform floor around them. 3. THE TV. A large 16:9 flat-screen TV hangs on the back of the moose glass wall, facing the viewer squarely, its screen one plain dark rectangle with a thin black bezel, nothing covering it. 4. A MINI MOOSE STATUE on the front desk: a small glossy white statue of a standing bull moose with broad antlers, like the moose on the glass wall, about as tall as the desk's monitor, standing on the reception desk's counter at the end of one of its curved wings, clearly visible beside the glass wall and not covered by it. Everything else stays as drawn: the frosted glass wall with the white ring and moose etched in it, the curved walnut reception desk beyond it, the round dark coffee table with its two curved coral-red sofas, the twin staircases, the offices, the front doors, the tall lancet windows, the yellow walls above dark oak Gothic wainscot, the honey plank floor and the brass lanterns hanging close to the walls. Keep every piece of furniture, the TV, the moose statue, the four computers and the front doors fully visible and unobstructed. Bright daytime light from the upper left. No people. Apart from the moose mark on the glass wall and the moose statue, no readable text, letters, numbers or logos anywhere.

Create one fully composed illustrated interior, 16:9: the front bar of the Side Project Cellar, a craft beer and spirits bar in Maplewood, St. Louis. The picture is about the wall of bottles behind the bar. Use reference 1 only for flat shape language and the bright palette. Use reference 2 (the real room) for the front bar: a long bar counter with a white subway-tile front and a dark walnut top; white square-tube metal bar stools with blond wood seats and backs; behind the counter a deep navy-blue wall with long floating dark-wood shelves on black iron brackets, a dark wood-framed mirror set into the wall, a row of dark wine bottles standing along the top of the wall, glass jar pendant lights with warm bulbs, black track lights, a polished warm-gray concrete floor. Use reference 3 (the real room) for the back bar: a rustic walk-in cooler enclosure clad in weathered pale and honey reclaimed planks, with a plank door, a few round beer-sign plaques, a black chalkboard framed in wood and a row of wine bottles along its top, black metal shelves of glassware beside it, blue-gray walls. Use reference 4 (this project's approved computer-lab illustration) for the rendering, edge quality and level of detail, so this room belongs to the same set of interiors; do NOT copy its furniture, walls or colours. Use reference 5 for the ten brand logos. CAMERA: a gentle three-quarter view, in the same flat isometric-style illustration: parallel projection with no vanishing points, verticals stay vertical. The camera stands raised in front of the front bar, looking down at about 30 degrees, turned only slightly, so the navy bar wall is seen almost face-on across the left three-quarters of the image, rising only gently toward the right. At the right the room turns a corner: the RIGHT wall recedes steeply toward the viewer and holds the back bar, seen at an angle. The near walls and ceiling are removed; the floor runs off the bottom edge and the walls rise to the top edge, no empty backdrop. Every object obeys this one grid. ROOM, exactly these fixtures: - THE TEN BRAND BOTTLES, the stars of the picture: all ten in one row on the long lower floating shelf across the middle of the navy wall, above the counter. They are clearly bigger, brighter and more detailed than every other bottle, standing upright, facing the viewer, evenly spaced with a clear gap of navy wall between neighbours, none overlapping another bottle or anything else, lit by a warm light strip under the shelf above so they glow against the navy wall. In this order from left to right, each carrying its brand's logo from reference 5 on its label, simplified but recognisable: 1 BACARDÍ rum, a clear square-shouldered bottle of pale gold rum, white label with the gold bat emblem over the black BACARDÍ wordmark; 2 GREY GOOSE vodka, a tall frosted white bottle with the blue flying geese and GREY GOOSE in blue; 3 NEW AMSTERDAM vodka, a tall slim clear bottle with a navy label, the white skyline mark and NEW AMSTERDAM; 4 CAMARENA tequila, a clear bottle with a black label lettered CAMARENA in white serif capitals; 5 BAREFOOT wine, a dark green wine bottle with a white label, the purple footprint and BAREFOOT in purple; 6 BUD LIGHT, a brown longneck beer bottle with a white label and BUD LIGHT in royal blue; 7 E&J brandy, an amber bottle with a black label and the white-and-gold E&J monogram; 8 PINK WHITNEY, a pale pink bottle with a black band lettered PINK WHITNEY; 9 RUMCHATA, a cream-white bottle lettered RumChata in brown-gold western capitals; 10 SOONHARI, a small green soju bottle with a black label lettered SOON HARI in white. Every other bottle (the wine bottles along the tops of the walls, a few plain whiskey bottles at the shelf ends) is smaller, darker and simpler, with no readable label, so the ten brand bottles stand out. - THE FRONT BAR: the counter runs parallel to the navy wall in front of it, with a narrow floor for the bartender between; its top stays below the brand bottles' shelf, so it never covers them. Six white stools stand in a row in front of the counter, evenly spaced, facing the bar, each standing on the floor. - THE BACK BAR: the reclaimed-wood cooler stands against the receding RIGHT wall, beyond the end of the front bar; only part of the back bar shows, its blank black chalkboard (nothing written on it) fully visible, a short second counter with a white subway-tile front in front of the cooler, and the glassware shelves beside it. - THE EXIT: a dark wood panel door with a brass handle at the far left end of the navy wall, just past the end of the counter, standing on the floor with clear floor in front of it. - The open concrete floor in front of the stools is clear for walking. Keep the ten brand bottles, the chalkboard and the exit door fully visible and unobstructed: no stool, counter, pendant light, wall edge or image edge covers any part of them. Bright daytime light from the upper left; the palette of reference 1 with the real room's colours: deep navy and blue-gray walls, white tile, white stools, blond and honey wood, warm gray concrete, turquoise and cyan accents. No people. Apart from the ten brand labels, no readable text, letters, numbers or logos anywhere.

Create one fully composed illustrated interior, 16:9: Brennan's, a cigar and cocktail bar on North Euclid in the Central West End, St. Louis. The picture is about the humidor and the five cigar brand boxes inside it. Use reference 1 only for flat shape language and the bright palette. Use reference 2 (the real room) for the humidor: a tall wall cabinet of dark wood-framed glass doors with warm-lit pale cedar shelves inside. Use reference 3 (the real room) for the rest of Brennan's: a rich teal painted paneled wall with built-in open bookshelves holding books, small objects and framed pictures; a long caramel leather banquette with small cream tables; exposed red brick; a cream pressed-tin ceiling; white paper globe pendant lamps. Use reference 4 (this project's approved three-quarter bar illustration) for the rendering, edge quality and level of detail, so this room belongs to the same set of interiors; do NOT copy its furniture, walls or colours. Use reference 5 for the five cigar brand logos and the Scandinavian Tobacco Group mark. CAMERA: a gentle three-quarter view, in the same flat isometric-style illustration: parallel projection with no vanishing points, verticals stay vertical. The camera stands raised in front of the humidor, looking down at about 30 degrees, turned only slightly, so the red-brick humidor wall is seen almost face-on across the left three-quarters of the image. At the right the room turns a corner: the RIGHT wall recedes steeply toward the viewer and is the teal paneled wall with its built-in bookshelves and framed pictures, the caramel leather banquette running along its foot with two or three small cream tables. The near walls are removed; a narrow band of the cream pressed-tin ceiling shows along the top edge; the floor runs off the bottom edge and the walls rise to the top, no empty backdrop. Every object obeys this one grid. ROOM, exactly these fixtures: - THE HUMIDOR: in the middle of the face-on brick wall, a tall dark wood cabinet built into the red-brick wall from the floor to about three-quarters of the wall's height, with glass doors in slim dark frames and warm-lit pale cedar shelves inside. Beside the humidor, the brick wall carries one large framed photograph. - THE FIVE BRAND CIGAR BOXES, the stars of the picture: display boxes much larger than real ones, each lid roughly one-tenth of the image width, all five in one row on the humidor's middle shelf at eye level, one box behind each of five tall glass doors. Each box stands upright on a small display easel with its lid facing the viewer, lit by a warm light strip, with a clear gap of pale cedar between neighbours, none overlapping another box or anything else. In this order, each lid carrying its brand's logo from reference 5, simplified but recognisable: 1 COHIBA, a glossy black lacquered box, its lid a cream label lettered COHIBA in heavy black capitals with the O filled red; 2 MACANUDO, a pale cedar box, its lid label the gold crown over the red-and-gold M crest with the small green PP seal, MACANUDO in black serif capitals below; 3 PARTAGAS, a black box lid with the white twin crowned shields and PARTAGAS in white capitals; 4 LA GLORIA CUBANA, a cream box lid lettered LA GLORIA CUBANA in black capitals in a gentle arch; 5 PUNCH, a warm cedar box, its lid the black crowned shield with a red scroll banner lettered PUNCH in black. Every other cigar box in the humidor (small plain boxes stacked flat on the shelves above and below) is smaller, darker and simpler, with no readable label, so the five brand boxes stand out. - THE STG PLAQUE: centred on the humidor's dark wood crown above the doors, a white plaque with the grey heraldic lion of reference 5 and a thin red base bar, SCANDINAVIAN TOBACCO GROUP in small dark capitals beneath it, the parent company over its brands. - THE LOUNGE: at the lower right in front of the banquette, well clear of the humidor; a caramel leather sofa, a dark wood low coffee table and one cream molded lounge chair on a teal rug, all standing on the floor, low enough that they never cover any part of the humidor's brand boxes. - THE EXIT: Brennan's front door, a dark teal door with a glass pane and a transom window above it, at the far left end of the brick wall, standing on the floor with clear floor in front of it. Keep the five brand boxes, the STG plaque and the exit door fully visible and unobstructed: no furniture, pendant lamp, wall edge or image edge covers any part of them. White paper globe pendant lamps hang only where they cover nothing. Medium cool-gray floor. Bright daytime light from the upper left; the palette of reference 1 with the real room's colours: rich teal and dark teal paneling, cream, red brick, caramel leather, pale cedar and dark wood, coral and golden-yellow accents. No people, no ATM. Apart from the five box lids and the STG plaque, no readable text, letters, numbers or logos anywhere.

EDIT the FINAL reference image. It is draft A1 of the small Alamo Drafthouse auditorium at City Foundry, the approved composition. Keep its true isometric camera and exact framing, the two back walls and back corner, the burnt-orange acoustic panels and cream light columns, the wall speakers, the three framed posters (Fast Five, Snow White and the Huntsman, The Lorax) with their artwork and titles, their size and position on the left wall, the exit door and its green exit sign, the screen with its black curtain surround, the projector ledge with its railing at the lower left, and the three rows of charcoal recliners with their tray tables: the same number of seats, the same size, angle and place in the image.
